sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Worth County?
sections.html:
Worth County runs billing and valuation through different offices. The assessors alone set what a parcel is worth, and the elected tax commissioner, who answers to neither the assessors nor the county commissioners, mails the statements. Sellers need the payoff from one and the value history from the other.

Worth County was carved out of Dooly and Irwin counties in December 1853 and became Georgia's 106th county. Sylvester serves as seat and as biggest city. Parts of Worth were later used to form Tift and Turner counties in 1905. Wikipedia credits cotton, peanuts and poultry as the economic base, and places Worth inside the Albany metropolitan area. The county spans 575 square miles, with Poulan, Warwick and the town of Sumner alongside Sylvester, and Acree, Bridgeboro and Oakfield as unincorporated communities.

On sales, the state rule is short: the January 1 owner owes the year, and a March or June closing returns nothing. Build the closing statement with that in mind.

sections.h2: Which Worth County office should I call?
sections.html:
Call the tax commissioner for bills and payoffs, and call the assessors for values, returns and exemptions.

Worth County property tax contacts and what each one answers
OfficeQuestions it handlesContact
Tax CommissionerBilling, payments, payoff figures, liens, tags201 N. Main St., Room 15, Sylvester, GA 31791; (229) 776-8204; Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30
Board of Tax AssessorsProperty values, returns, appeals, homestead(229) 776-8203
Board of CommissionersMillage, solid waste fee waivers(229) 776-8200, extension 1
Clerk of CourtsCopies of your warranty deedFirst floor of the county courthouse

Payment options on the tax site include paying online, mailing a check to the Room 15 address, calling in a payment, and using the drop box in the alley between the courthouse and the jail.

sections.h2: When is the Worth County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
On the tax office's FAQ, land, buildings and business property are paid in two parts, one due October 15 and the other November 15. Manufactured homes follow an April 1 date instead. Weekend deadlines roll to Monday.

Because schedules can move with the digest, treat the date on your own statement as final, and phone the office if a closing lands near a deadline.

Statewide, the revenue department's default is December 20 unless a local government moves it, with interest held off until 60 days past the bill's postmark. Request the exact late charges along with your payoff.

  • Only a USPS-dated postmark proves a payment was on time. A meter stamp is rejected.
  • The office takes installments of any size, yet charges keep growing on the unpaid remainder.
  • Statements are mailed to the homeowner and never to the lender. Mortgage companies receive a data file, so forward your bill if escrow pays it.

sections.h2: What is the solid waste fee on a Worth County tax bill?
sections.html:
Any residential or business structure outside the cities carries an annual $264.00 solid waste fee, added to the same bill. The Board of Commissioners adopted this by resolution beginning in 2019.

Two relief paths exist. If a structure is dilapidated or vacant for the entire year, the owner can file a waiver request for the Board of Commissioners to approve. Owners over 65 whose total household income is $15,200 or less can qualify for an elderly exemption by completing an affidavit at the commissioners' office, reachable at (229) 776-8200, extension 1.

This matters in a sale because an inherited or empty rural house may carry the fee even when nobody has lived there. Ask whether a waiver was ever filed, and include any unpaid fee in the payoff figure.

sections.h2: What is the process to contest a Worth County value?
sections.html:
Your written appeal must reach the assessors within 45 days of the date printed on the notice. State the grounds (taxability, value, uniformity, or a refused exemption) and name the route you want.

Before April 1 each year, owners may file a return stating a preferred value. The assessors review it and, if they disagree, mail a notice carrying their figure, which starts the clock. Questions about the form go to (229) 776-8203.

The three routes are the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue staff oversee the process but cannot reverse a single parcel's outcome. Any refund from a final value is processed automatically.

sections.h2: How do homestead and other exemptions work in Worth County?
sections.html:
Homestead status requires owning and occupying the house on New Year's Day, and the assessors' office approves each application. Forms can arrive in any month, though April 1 is the last day that helps the current bill.

Approval rolls forward each year while you stay put. A move or a deed change restarts the process, so a buyer files fresh after closing.

Other programs the county tax site mentions:

  • The freeport exemption for business personal property, handled by the assessors.
  • Special assessment programs, which the assessors can describe by phone.
  • The elderly exemption from the solid waste fee described above.

sections.h2: What if taxes are late or a lien is recorded in Worth County?
sections.html:
A 30-day warning letter goes out before any lien is filed. The lien, a FiFa, lands on the court's General Execution Docket, held by the superior court clerk, once a balance passes 90 days late, and because the entry is public, credit bureaus may pick it up.

Full payment of tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. Liens are not sold over the counter here. Once a levy and tax sale advertisement begin, the office urges walking the payment in.

Manufactured and modular homes count as personal property, and the location permit is withheld until the current mobile home tax is paid in full. A seller with one on the lot should settle that account first.

sections.h2: Which Worth County housing figures matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 20,784 people in 2020 and estimates 20,059 for July 2025. Its 2020 to 2024 table lists a $104,900 median home value, owners in 73.7% of houses, and 7,739 households. Rent averages a median $864, and the median household earns $58,694. Builders took out 61 permits in 2025.

That census recorded 9,244 housing units, 11.5% of them vacant, and found 29.6% of people in urban areas. Workers travel an average of 28.4 minutes to their jobs. The county borders Dougherty, Lee, Crisp, Turner, Tift, Colquitt and Mitchell counties.

The population peaked at 23,863 in the 1920 census and has fallen to the 2020 count. Broadband reaches 74.5% of households, a bachelor's degree is held by 11.7% of adults, and the poverty rate is 26.4%. Retail sales were $8,567 per resident in 2022, and employers numbered 288 in 2023, with 2,375 jobs. The county lists 1,186 veterans. The number that controls your sale is still the payoff the tax commissioner gives you, together with the value on your assessment notice.

faqs.q: Where is the Worth County tax office?
faqs.a: At 201 N. Main St., Room 15 in Sylvester, or by phone at (229) 776-8204, online, through the mail, or at the drop box in the alley beside the jail.

faqs.q: What are the Worth County tax due dates?
faqs.a: October 15 and November 15 for land and buildings, and April 1 for mobile homes, per the tax FAQ. Your bill has the final word.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to dispute a Worth County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counting from the notice. Call the assessors at (229) 776-8203 for the form.

faqs.q: Does the solid waste fee apply to a vacant house?
faqs.a: It can, though a structure dilapidated or empty all year may earn a waiver. The commissioners' office at (229) 776-8200, extension 1 decides.

faqs.q: Will a late payment hurt my credit?
faqs.a: Only if a lien is recorded, which can follow a balance more than 90 days late. The tax office itself reports nothing to credit bureaus.
